statement: Respect the problem boundary you have established: a component declared a black box (here the data science team that computes the top 100 photos) is not yours to design - do not assume or redesign how it works; you own only your page.
detail: Said twice to students who started designing the top-100 computation: at 01:58:52 ('We don't have to care. That's what I said. Why are you assuming?') and at 02:19:52-02:20:05 ('black box for us, data science does it. We don't care how they do it.' ... 'We are the owner of this page. That is a black box for us.').
case_study: Hashtag service: the top 100 photos per hashtag come from the data science team's service.
speaker: teacher
verbatim: Why are you assuming? We said, we established the boundary, data science team is doing it for us, right?

statement: A student assumed that because Kafka is a replicated cluster, its uptime is 'all the time' and it never goes down; the teacher corrected this: Kafka can go down.
detail: The teacher's correction: 'No, no, it can go down.' Kafka gives 99.9% availability, not four or five nines, and writes made while it is down are lost unless you handle them (dead letter queue, buffer in memory, or accept the loss).
speaker: student (proposal)
verbatim: So uptime is uptime is all the time. It doesn't go down even for any time.
